```{r importdata, warning=FALSE}
library(tidyverse)

AccaData<- read.csv("Results.csv") #import data
AccaData$Date<- as.Date(AccaData$Date, format = "%d/%m/%Y") #format date properly
AccaData$Odds<- as.numeric(format(AccaData$Odds, digits = 3))
#AccaData$Win<- as.factor(AccaData$Win) #wanted to make this a factor but the summary uses sum() which only works on numeric data
AccaData$HomeAway<- as.factor(AccaData$HomeAway)

TotalWinnings<- 3795+1509+200
```


Keeping track of our team acca and looking at trends. Data covers the period between `r min(AccaData$Date)` and `r max(AccaData$Date)` and the gladiators playing are: `r unique(AccaData$Player)`. **That one time our acca actually came in (for £3795 on 16/09/2023) was before data was being collected. On 29/3/2025, Doug cashed out for £1509. It was the correct decision as Leeds went on to draw and the bet would have lost. After 4 postponements for frozen pitches on 3/1/2026, Doug cashed out for £199.88. It was the correct decision as Man City went on to draw and the (abridged) bet would have lost.**

> Our winnings so far total is... **£`r TotalWinnings`**

# Stats as a group

As a group, our overall win rate between `r min(AccaData$Date)` and `r max(AccaData$Date)` is **`r format(sum(AccaData$Win, na.rm = TRUE)/length(AccaData$Win)*100, digits = 2)`%** including `r sum(AccaData$EarlyPayout == 1, na.rm = TRUE)` (`r format(sum(AccaData$EarlyPayout == 1, na.rm = TRUE)/nrow(AccaData)*100, digits = 1)`%) games won with the early payout offer (when a team goes 2 goals up so the bet wins but the team draws or loses). As a group, we have backed `r length(unique(AccaData$Team))` different teams. Our most popular team to bet on is **`r names(which.max(table(AccaData$Team)))`**. Our most popular team to bet against is **`r names(which.max(table(AccaData$Against)))`**. The average odds for a bet are **`r format(mean(AccaData$Odds), digits = 3)`** ([converter to fractions if wanted](https://www.aceodds.com/bet-calculator/odds-converter.html)). Our biggest odds winning bet ever was by **`r AccaData[AccaData$Win == 1,] %>% filter(Odds == max(Odds, na.rm = TRUE)) %>% select(Player)`** when they bet on `r AccaData[AccaData$Win == 1,] %>% filter(Odds == max(Odds, na.rm = TRUE)) %>% select(Team)` to beat `r AccaData[AccaData$Win == 1,] %>% filter(Odds == max(Odds, na.rm = TRUE)) %>% select(Against)` at odds of `r AccaData[AccaData$Win == 1,] %>% filter(Odds == max(Odds, na.rm = TRUE)) %>% select(Odds)`. The softest of bets (unsurprisingly) came from **`r AccaData[AccaData$Odds == min(AccaData$Odds),"Player"]`** when they bet on `r AccaData[AccaData$Odds == min(AccaData$Odds, na.rm = TRUE),"Team"]` to beat `r AccaData[AccaData$Odds == min(AccaData$Odds),"Against"]` at odds of `r AccaData[AccaData$Odds == min(AccaData$Odds),"Odds"]` - the bet `r ifelse(AccaData[AccaData$Odds == min(AccaData$Odds, na.rm = TRUE),"Win"] == 1, "won", "lost")`: was it *really* worth it? **`r AccaData$Player[AccaData$Odds == min(AccaData$Odds[AccaData$Win == 0], na.rm = TRUE) & AccaData$Win == 0]`** has the lowest odds bet to lose (`r min(AccaData$Odds[AccaData$Win == 0], na.rm = TRUE)`) - what a guy.

## Success (or lack thereof) tracker

```{r timetracker, warning=FALSE, out.width='100%'}
#AccaData %>% group_by(Date) %>% summarise(Wins = sum(Win), Odds = prod(Odds)) %>% ggplot(aes(x = Date)) + geom_bar(aes(y = Wins, fill = Date), stat = "identity") + geom_smooth(aes(y = Odds/70), stat = "identity") + theme_classic() + theme(legend.position = "none") + labs(title = "Weekly tracker", subtitle = "Bars for Wins (left axis), line for Total Odds (right axis)") + scale_y_continuous(breaks = 1:11, sec.axis = sec_axis(name = "Odds", transform = ~.*70)) #get summary of each acca. this plot adds a second axis and plots a line for odds. I prefer the second plot for simplicity of figure and code

GroupWins<- AccaData %>% group_by(Date) %>% summarise(Wins = sum(Win), Return = ceiling(11*prod(Odds)))

GroupWins %>% ggplot(aes(x = Date)) + geom_bar(aes(y = Wins, fill = Return), stat = "identity") + geom_text(aes(label=Return, y = Wins),vjust=-0.5, size = 2) + theme_classic() + labs(title = "Weekly tracker", subtitle = "Total estimated Return (£) from £11 stake shown above bar", caption = "bet365 boost odds on accas so the payout shown may be less than actual return on Doug's betslip") + ylim(c(0,11)) + scale_y_continuous(breaks = 0:11) + theme(panel.grid.major.y = element_line(linetype = 2)) #get summary of each acca

CloseCalls<- GroupWins %>% filter(Wins == 10 | Date == "2026-01-03") %>% mutate(CostinMincePies = ceiling(Return*0.5))
library(kableExtra)
cbind(AccaData[which(AccaData$Date %in% CloseCalls$Date & AccaData$Win == 0),1:6], CostofLoss = paste0("£",CloseCalls$Return), MincePiesLost = CloseCalls$CostinMincePies) %>% mutate(CostofLoss = ifelse(Date %in% c("2025-03-29", "2026-01-03"), yes = paste0(CostofLoss,"*"), no = CostofLoss)) %>% kbl(caption = "Table of shame. When we were one result away from the jackpot", row.names = FALSE) %>% kable_classic(html_font = "Cambria") %>% kable_styling("striped") %>% footnote(symbol_manual = "*", symbol = "An early cash out saved some of the money but none of the shame")
```

*The amount of mince pies we missed out on is calculated based on Tesco Finest 6 pack (clubcard price) bought in December 2025*

## Home/Away and Odds tracker

Tracker of the ratio of home/away picks and a histogram showing at what odds our winning (and losing) bets are placed. On 13/04/2025, Doug picked Birmingham to win at Wembley which is why there is one "Neutral" bit on the Home/Away plot (they lost by the way). Also any AFCON games picked have been marked as "Neutral" (but none of them won so it doesn't make any difference).

```{r homeaway, fig.show='hold', out.width='50%', warning=FALSE}
ggplot(data = AccaData, aes(x = as.character(Date), y = Win, fill = HomeAway)) + geom_bar(stat = "identity") + theme_classic() + labs(title = "Home/Away tracker") + scale_y_continuous(breaks = 1:11) + theme(axis.text.x = element_blank(), axis.title.x = element_blank()) #bar plot showing split of home or away picks for winning bets

#summary(lm(Win ~ Odds + HomeAway, data = AccaData)) #regression using odds and homeaway as predictors of win

ggplot(data = AccaData) + geom_histogram(aes(x = Odds, group = Win, fill = as.factor(Win)), binwidth = 0.1) + theme_classic() + labs(title = "Histogram of bets made at different odds", fill = "Win") + theme(legend.position = "inside", legend.position.inside = c(0.9,0.9)) + scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Dark2", direction = -1) #histogram showing success of bets at different odds. I think this plot could be a nice way of showing the sweet spot of odds
```

Who are our popular teams to back or go against?

```{r popularity, fig.show='hold', out.width='50%', warning=FALSE}
#popularity of teams
library(treemapify)
AccaData %>% group_by(Team) %>% summarise(Wins = sum(Win, na.rm = TRUE), Picked = n()) %>% mutate(Percent = Wins/Picked*100) %>% ggplot(aes(area = Picked, fill = Percent, label = paste(Team, Picked, sep = "\n"))) + geom_treemap() +   geom_treemap_text(place = "centre", aes(colour = after_scale(prismatic::best_contrast(fill, c("white", "black"))))) + theme(legend.position = "none") + labs(title = "Popular teams to bet on (the lighter the blue, the more wins)") + scale_fill_continuous()
#collapse teams picked once into a single category

AccaData %>% group_by(Against) %>% summarise(Wins = sum(Win, na.rm = TRUE), Picked = n()) %>% mutate(Percent = Wins/Picked*100) %>% ggplot(aes(area = Picked, fill = Percent, label = paste(Against, Picked, sep = "\n"))) + geom_treemap() +   geom_treemap_text(place = "centre", aes(colour = after_scale(prismatic::best_contrast(fill, c("white", "black"))))) + theme(legend.position = "none") + labs(title = "Popular teams to bet against (the lighter the blue, the more wins)") + scale_fill_continuous()
```

This plot does a similar thing but in two dimensions and with cool interactivity.

```{r interactivescatter, out.width='100%'}
TeamsScatter<- AccaData %>% group_by(Team) %>% summarise(AvgOdds = mean(Odds), PercentWin = as.numeric(format(sum(Win == 1, na.rm = TRUE)/length(Win)*100, digits = 2)), Bets = length(Win)) %>% ggplot(aes(x = AvgOdds, y = PercentWin, size = Bets, fill = Bets, text = Team)) + geom_point() + theme_minimal() + scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent_format(scale = 1)) + annotate("text", x = 1.25, y = 10, label = "Low odds\nand few wins", col = "#0d0887") + annotate("text", x = 3, y = 90, label = "High odds\nand more wins", col = "#f89540") + annotate("text", x = 3, y = 10, label = "High odds\nand few wins", col = "#7e03a8") + annotate("text", x = 1.25, y = 90, label = "Low odds\nand more wins", col = "#cc4778")

plotly::ggplotly(TeamsScatter)
```

```{r bogeyteams}
#are there any teams we've never won with/against?
Letdowns<- AccaData %>% group_by(Team) %>% summarise(Wins = sum(Win), Total = n()) %>% mutate(Percent = Wins/Total*100) %>% arrange(-Percent) %>% filter(Total > 2, Wins == 0)

BogeyTeams<- AccaData %>% group_by(Against) %>% summarise(Wins = sum(Win), Total = n()) %>% mutate(Percent = Wins/Total*100) %>% arrange(-Percent) %>% filter(Total > 1, Wins == 0)
```

Are we a curse on teams or are they a curse on us?! We've never won a bet (number of bets in brackets) on `r paste(paste(Letdowns$Team), paste0("(", Letdowns$Total, ")"), sep = ", ")`. Likewise, we've lost 100% of bets (number of bets in brackets) placed *against* `r paste(paste(BogeyTeams$Against), paste0("(", BogeyTeams$Total, ")"), sep = ", ")`

# Individual Stats

## Summary of each player (after `r length(unique(AccaData$Date))` picks)

```{r GroupTable}
#best way to present a lot of the data will be as a table
PlayerSummary<- AccaData %>% group_by(Player) %>% summarise(PercentWin = format(sum(Win, na.rm = TRUE)/length(Win)*100, digits = 2),
                                            Mean = format(mean(Odds), digits = 3),
                                            Median = format(median(Odds), digits = 3),
                                            Min = format(min(Odds), digits = 3),
                                            Max = format(max(Odds), digits = 3),
                                            PercentHome = format(sum(HomeAway == "H")/length(HomeAway)*100, digits = 2),
                                            DifferentTeams = length(unique(Team)),
                                            FavouriteTeam = paste0(names(which.max(table(Team))), " (",table(Team)[which.max(table(Team))], ")"),
                                            HatedTeam = paste0(names(which.max(table(Against))), " (",table(Against)[which.max(table(Against))], ")"))

DaysSinceWin<- AccaData %>% group_by(Player) %>% filter(Win == 1) %>% mutate(LastWin = last(Date) - last(AccaData$Date)) %>% distinct(Player, .keep_all = TRUE) #work out how many days since last win
PlayerSummary$LastWin<- DaysSinceWin$LastWin[match(x = PlayerSummary$Player, table = DaysSinceWin$Player)]

CurrentStreak<- AccaData %>% group_by(Player) %>% filter(Win == 0) %>% mutate(LastLoss = last(Date)) %>% select(c(Player, LastLoss)) %>% distinct(Player, .keep_all = TRUE) #work out when last loss was
CurrentStreak<- AccaData %>% group_by(Player) %>% left_join(y = CurrentStreak, by = "Player") %>% filter(Date > LastLoss) %>% mutate(Streak = sum(Win, na.rm = TRUE))

PlayerSummary$Streak<- CurrentStreak$Streak[match(x = PlayerSummary$Player, table = CurrentStreak$Player)]

#PlayerSummary<- cbind(PlayerSummary, Consistency = as.numeric(PlayerSummary$Min)/as.numeric(PlayerSummary$Max)

PlayerSummary<- PlayerSummary[order(as.numeric(PlayerSummary$PercentWin), decreasing = TRUE),] #order by win%

PlayerSummary %>% kbl(caption = "For Favourite and Hated teams, number of times picked is shown in brackets. If there is tie, the team first alphabetically is shown.") %>% kable_classic(html_font = "Cambria") %>% kable_styling("striped") %>% column_spec(3, background = spec_color(as.numeric(PlayerSummary$Mean), option = "plasma")) %>% column_spec(4, background = spec_color(as.numeric(PlayerSummary$Median), option = "C")) %>% column_spec(5, background = spec_color(as.numeric(PlayerSummary$Min), option = "C")) %>% column_spec(6, background = spec_color(as.numeric(PlayerSummary$Max), option = "C")) %>% column_spec(3:6, bold = FALSE, color = "lightgreen")
```

# Individual bet tracker

```{r playeroddsovertime, out.width='100%'}
#make a line plot of everyone's bet odds week by week

d<- plotly::highlight_key(AccaData, ~Player)

plotly::highlight(plotly::ggplotly(ggplot(data = d, aes(x = Date, y = Odds, col = Player, label = Team)) + geom_point(aes(shape = as.factor(Win))) + geom_line() + theme_classic() + geom_hline(yintercept = 2, lty = 2, alpha = 0.5) + labs(title = "Tracker of bet odds over time") + theme(legend.position = "none")), on = "plotly_click", off = "plotly_relayout", color = "black", opacityDim = 0.3)

print("Click on a data point to see that player's trend (hold shift key for multiple selections. The dotted line represents evens")
```

# *What you could have won...*

What if you just placed a £1 stake on your selection every week instead? How many £££s would you be up (or down)?

```{r bettally}
Tally<- AccaData[AccaData$Win == 1 & !is.na(AccaData$Win),] %>% group_by(Player) %>% summarise(Total = sum(Odds)) %>% mutate(Winnings = Total - length(unique(AccaData$Date)))# %>% select(-2)

Tally<- Tally[order(as.numeric(Tally$Winnings), decreasing = TRUE),] #order by win%

#Tally$Winnings <- paste0("\u00A3", Tally$Winnings) #trying to add £ for nice readability but caused issues

Tally[-2] %>% kbl(caption = "What if you went it alone?", align = "lc", table.attr = "style='width:30%;'") %>% kable_classic(html_font = "Cambria") %>% kable_styling("striped") %>% column_spec(2, color = "white", background = ifelse(Tally$Winnings < 0, "red", "green"))
```


```{r predictiveness, eval=FALSE, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
#Multiple ROC curves. One for players, one for home/away, one for stratified odds?
#having difficulty with this. I'm not sure the curves are exactly what I am expecting to show. It is difficult to make a roc curve with only one outcome (ie there are no "controls", for 100% of rows the outcome is a "case"/win. There can be no false positives!)
#this could be an alternative: https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/COINr/vignettes/sensitivity.html

cor(x = AccaData$Odds, y = AccaData$Win) #correlation between odds and outcome. negative value means that the lower the odds, the more likely a win (which is what would be expected).

library(pROC)

AccaModel<- lapply(unique(AccaData$Player), function(x) glm(Win ~ Odds, data = AccaData[which(AccaData$Player == x),])) #regression using odds and homeaway as predictors of win
names(AccaModel)<- unique(AccaData$Player)
for(player in names(AccaModel)){
  print(player)
  print(ggroc(roc(AccaModel[[player]][["y"]], predict(AccaModel[[player]], type = "response"))) + geom_abline(intercept = 1, linetype = 2) + theme_classic() + labs(title = paste(player))) + labs(x = "False Positive Rate", y = "True Positive Rate") #ROC curve for model
}

#precision recall curves are more suited to the question being asked here

library(yardstick) #package for PR curves


AccaData$Truth<- as.factor(1) #Positive Predictive Power = True Positives / (True Positives + False Positives). False positives are impossible!
Recall <- sum(AccaData$Win == 1) / (sum(AccaData$Win == 1) + sum(AccaData$Win == 0))

#AccaData %>% group_by(Player) %>% pr_curve(Truth, Win) %>% autoplot()
```
